brief.subject: FBI warns of midterm election scams, plus a sextortion crackdown
brief.headline: FBI Flags Midterm Election Scams; FTC Halts Alleged Sextortion 'Relief' Scheme
brief.dek: Election-season fraud warnings, a court halt on a sextortion help firm, $9.8 million in wire-fraud refunds, and a ticket broker lawsuit.
brief.lede: The FBI says scammers are exploiting the 2026 midterm election to run multiple fraud schemes. Expect political-season pitches to keep coming as November nears.

sections.heading: Midterm Election Scams on the Rise
bullets: The FBI warned on Oct. 15 that scammers are using the 2026 midterm election to run multiple fraud schemes.
A separate FBI alert cautions voters about election crimes ahead of the November vote.
Election season brings a flood of calls, texts and emails, which gives fraudsters cover to blend in.
Verify any election-related request before sharing money or personal details.

sections.heading: Sextortion 'Help' Firm Halted
bullets: A federal court temporarily halted Digital Forensics Corporation LLC and its CEO at the FTC's request.
The FTC alleges the firm took millions of dollars with false promises to identify sextortion criminals and stop attacks.
The FTC calls sextortion a rapidly growing threat, often run by foreign scammers.
Victims in a panic can be targeted a second time by paid 'rescue' services that overpromise.

sections.heading: $9.8 Million Back for Wire-Fraud Victims
bullets: The FTC is sending more than $9.8 million to consumers harmed through Walmart's wire transfer services.
Scammers used those services to take hundreds of millions of dollars from U.S. consumers, according to the FTC.
Walmart settled FTC charges in June 2025 over allegedly weak anti-fraud policies and staff training.
Wire transfers are a favorite scam payment method because money is hard to recover once sent.

sections.heading: Ticket Broker Sued Over Bulk Buying
bullets: The FTC sued REPS & Company Inc., alleging it dodged limits on how many tickets one buyer can purchase.
The broker allegedly bought millions of tickets to high-demand events and resold them at a significant profit.
Such tactics can leave fans paying inflated resale prices for popular shows.

brief.seo_description: FBI warns of 2026 midterm election scams, FTC halts an alleged sextortion relief scheme, and $9.8 million goes to wire-fraud victims.
